title: Chest Pain Differential Diagnosis
description: Differential diagnosis for acute chest pain in adults, covering cardiac, pulmonary, GI, and musculoskeletal etiologies.
source_description: 2021 AHA/ACC/ASE/CHEST/SAEM/SCCT/SCMR Guideline for the Evaluation and Diagnosis of Chest Pain. Gulati M, et al. JACC 2021;78(22):e187-e285.

diagnoses.name: Acute Coronary Syndrome (ACS)
key_features: Radiation to left arm, jaw, or back

diagnoses.name: Esophageal Rupture (Boerhaave Syndrome)
key_features: Severe chest/epigastric pain after forceful vomiting
Mackler triad: vomiting, chest pain, subcutaneous emphysema

diagnoses.name: Gastroesophageal Reflux (GERD)
key_features: Worse after meals or lying down
recommended_tests: ECG to rule out cardiac cause first

diagnoses.name: Musculoskeletal / Costochondritis
recommended_tests: ECG to rule out cardiac cause first

also_consider.name: Takotsubo (Stress) Cardiomyopathy
also_consider.rationale: Mimics ACS especially in post-menopausal women after emotional/physical stress; normal coronaries on catheterization

also_consider.name: Herpes Zoster (Pre-Rash Phase)
also_consider.rationale: Dermatomal chest pain precedes vesicular rash by 2-3 days; can mimic ACS or PE before rash appears

also_consider.name: Pleuritis (Non-PE)
also_consider.rationale: Sharp pleuritic pain associated with viral URI or autoimmune disease; diagnosis of exclusion after PE ruled out

also_consider.name: Pulmonary Hypertension
also_consider.rationale: Exertional chest tightness with progressive dyspnea; check echocardiography for elevated RVSP

also_consider.name: Esophageal Spasm
also_consider.rationale: Mimics angina closely and may respond to nitroglycerin, creating diagnostic confusion; consider if cardiac workup negative

also_consider.name: Biliary Colic
also_consider.rationale: Epigastric or RUQ pain radiating to chest, post-prandial; check RUQ ultrasound

also_consider.name: Panic Disorder
also_consider.rationale: Chest pain with hyperventilation and paresthesias; diagnosis of exclusion after cardiac workup

also_consider.name: Acute Chest Syndrome (Sickle Cell Disease)
also_consider.rationale: Chest pain with fever and new pulmonary infiltrate in sickle cell patients; medical emergency

also_consider.name: Cocaine-Induced Coronary Vasospasm
also_consider.rationale: Coronary vasospasm causing ACS-like presentation; always ask about substance use in young adults with chest pain

also_consider.name: Tietze Syndrome
also_consider.rationale: Painful swelling of costochondral junction; distinguished from costochondritis by visible swelling on exam

clinical_reasoning_prompt: This is an evidence-based reference set, not an exhaustive differential. Consider atypical presentations (especially in women, diabetics, and elderly), substance use history, recent procedures or trauma, and diagnoses not listed here. Always exclude life-threatening causes before considering benign etiologies. A normal ECG and troponin do not exclude ACS — serial evaluation may be required.
